newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's governing alliance shows strain on Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy's governing alliance shows strain on Albania.

text.p: Relations between Italy's centre-left government and its key allies showed fresh signs of strain on Wednesday over the planned deployment of an Italian-led force to secure humanitarian relief to Albania.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, addressing the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) after his ally the hard-left Communist Refoundation party opposed the mission, appealed for all sides to pull together for the sake of "higher national interests".
Franco Marini, leader of the centre-left Popular Party, said the government was showing scant cohesion.
The main centre-right opposition parties have pledged to support the security force.

Marini told the Chamber the governing alliance "can't manage to hold convincingly even on the big questions". The centre-left won an historic election victory last April and Prodi's government is due to celebrate its first birthday next month.

The Greens party, a government member, laid down a string of conditions it wants attached to the deployment of a multinational force some 5,000-strong which Italy hopes can begin its mission to the chaotic Balkan state next week.

The Greens want to make sure the force plays a purely humanitarian role and for Italian patrols of the Adriatic to deter refugee-seekers to stop. Some 13,000 have already fled to Italy by sea since armed lawlessness spread across Albania following the collapse of shady investment schemes in January.
The Senate (upper house) and the Chamber of Deputies are both expected to vote this week on deployment of the force.

"Anyone denying (the government) support will be taking on a very serious political responsibility," said Massimo D'Alema, whose ex-communist Democratic Party of the Left is the biggest force in Prodi's government.

Communist Refoundation, which has a fractious relationship with the government but whose support ensures Prodi a majority in the lower house, has said conditions did not exist to send troops to Albania.
It says the sinking of a boat packed with Albanian refugees after a collision with an Italian navy ship has incited anti-Italian hostility in Albania.
